claims.statement: Orders allocated overnight to east node are stuck in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' state, with all affected orders flagged as split-reservation exceptions by the allocation system.
claims.corroboration: Alert (m8_e02, tier-1) confirms 9% of overnight allocations held on east-node lanes since 06:00; fulfilment report (m8_e10, tier-2) confirms all held orders flagged as split-reservation exceptions.
claims.limitation: Observation confirms the symptom (stuck orders + split-reservation flags) but not the mechanism. Split-reservation exceptions could indicate a rule defect, insufficient inventory at east node, or a carrier-side failure to acknowledge.

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18, deployed at 22:00, changed east-node stock reservation priority for multi-node orders and may be causally related to the morning allocation failures.
claims.corroboration: Timing: rule went live 8 hours before stuck orders appeared (06:00). Pattern specificity: stuck orders limited to east node, matching the scope of v18 change (east-node priority for multi-node orders).
claims.limitation: Timing correlation is not causation. Change review passed and regression suite was green; those tests may not cover overnight multi-node allocations under the new east-node-first logic. No evidence yet of the specific defect.

claims.statement: Carrier-side systems have a confirmation lag or are not acknowledging pickup availability for the subset of orders waiting on the east-node feed.
claims.corroboration: Observability gap (m8_e09, tier-1) confirms internal dashboards cannot see how booked pickups relate to carrier-side confirmations. Carrier Ops initial check did not identify dock/schedule issues.
claims.limitation: No direct evidence of carrier system failure. Requires trace of carrier integration logs and confirmation handoff to rule in/out.

capability_gaps.reason: Cannot discriminate between allocation-rule-defect (v18 bug causing invalid splits) and carrier-feed-lag (valid allocations but carrier not picking up) without tracing the handoff from booked pickup to carrier-side confirmation.

next_action.rationale: Determine whether split-reservation exceptions are logically correct given v18 rule (inventory legitimately insufficient at east node to fulfill orders) or whether v18 has a defect (reserving incorrectly, failing to try fallback nodes). Discriminates between allocation-rule-defect and carrier-feed-lag hypotheses.
next_action.expected_information_gain: If v18 is correctly splitting across nodes but carriers are not collecting, points to carrier-side issue. If v18 is incorrectly refusing to split or mis-reserving stock, points to rule defect in v18.
